name: Cornelius
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: Cornelius was a centurion of the Italian band, a devout man that feared God with all his house. Where was he from? Caesarea. On the map, Caesarea sits right above Samaria: that's Manasseh's land. Cornelius was northern kingdom, not a Gentile of the nations. Do some research; do some study.
There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band. Caesarea, named after Caesar, was on the north coast of the land of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: Cornelius was of the Italian band, a Roman army unit, not of Italian blood. Israelites served in Rome's army as they serve in America's today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian band. When our people read "Italian band" they automatically picture a Caucasian, but Caesarea Maritima sat on a seacoast in the land of Israel, and Cornelius was an Israelite officer in the Roman army, not a man of another nation.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Cornelius saw in a vision about the ninth hour an angel of the Most High who told him his prayers and his alms were come up for a memorial before God. The Most High only regards the prayer of Zion, the destitute, the prisoner, so this hearing of Cornelius marks him as Israel.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: The angel sends Cornelius to Joppa for Simon called Peter, lodging with Simon a tanner by the seaside, who will tell him what he ought to do. When the angel departed, Cornelius called two household servants and a devout soldier who waited on him.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: This was done thrice, and the vessel was received up again into heaven. While Peter doubted in himself what the vision meant, the men sent from Cornelius had already found Simon's house and stood before the gate, asking whether Simon called Peter lodged there.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Write this down: Caesarea is in the land of Israel; it is in the land of West Manasseh, right beside Samaria. Map shown on screen. Deacon: Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport there; he sailed up north to visit Cornelius. Christ was raised further up, Galilee, so he was raised around them in that area. And that place Scythopolis means city of the Scythians; Scythians is northern kingdom also. That's who Paul wrote to in Colossians 3:11.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: The men from Cornelius told Peter: Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by an holy angel to send for thee.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit told him three men were seeking him and to go with them, doubting nothing, for the Most High had sent them. The men reported that Cornelius the centurion, a just man that feareth God and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned by a holy angel to send for Peter.

Cornelius is now called a just man, adding to devout from verse 2, and to be just is to keep the law that is holy, just, and good. Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him, so they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: The next day they entered Caesarea, and Cornelius, who had gathered his kinsmen and near friends, met Peter, fell down at his feet, and worshipped him. Peter took him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself also am a man," refusing the worship, and went in to find many come together.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Cornelius rehearses the events: four days ago at the ninth hour he was praying and fasting when a man stood before him in bright clothing, an angel, and told him his prayer was heard and his alms had in remembrance in the sight of the Most High. This shows our alms and prayers are regarded and counted as a memorial before the Most High.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In
